article.title: Claude Sonnet 5.5 is 2 points behind Opus 5.5 at half the price per token, with one catch
article.preview_text:
Claude Sonnet 5.5 came out today on 28 September.
On GDPval-AA, Anthropic's benchmark for real knowledge work, it scores 1844. Opus 5.5 scores 1846. On the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index it

blocks.text: Claude Sonnet 5.5 came out today on 28 September.

On GDPval-AA, Anthropic's benchmark for real knowledge work, it scores 1844. Opus 5.5 scores 1846. On the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index it scores 56 against 58. It costs half as much per token.
There is one catch. It changes what you pay.

I ran it on launch day to see what all of this means if you make content for a living. This is everything I found. The benchmarks, the catch, where the model slips, and a live test on real TikTok, Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts data.
Bookmark this one. It has three prompts to run this week, and five hooks for posting about Sonnet 5.5 while the news is fresh.
What's inside
- How close Sonnet 5.5 gets to Opus 5.5
- The catch, and how to avoid it
- Where it slips, according to Anthropic's own system card
- A live test on hooks that name Claude, and on what happened to Opus 5.5 launch week
- Five hooks Sonnet 5.5 wrote for this week's news
- Three prompts to run the test yourself
How close Sonnet 5.5 gets to Opus 5.5
Sonnet 5.5 is the second model in the Claude 5.5 family. Opus 5.5 came out on 22 September, and Anthropic says Haiku 5.5 follows in the coming weeks.

The price is $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, the same as Sonnet 5. Opus 5.5 is $4 and $20. Anthropic also says Sonnet 5.5 generates output more than 30% faster than Sonnet 5, and costs up to 30% less per task.
Here is how it does against Opus 5.5 on Anthropic's own numbers.
- GDPval-AA, real work across 44 occupations. Sonnet 5 scored 1449. Sonnet 5.5 scores 1844. Opus 5.5 scores 1846.
- Terminal-Bench 4.0, multi-step work in a command line. Sonnet 5.5 scores 70.6% and Sonnet 5 scored 10.3%. Opus 5.5 scores 66.4%, so the cheaper model is ahead.
- CursorBench 4.0, tasks from real Cursor coding sessions. Sonnet 5.5 scores 55.5% against 57.8% for Opus 5.5.
- OSWorld 2.1, computer use. 80.1% against 81.8%.
- FrontierCode 1.1, which asks whether an agent's code change would get merged. This is the biggest gap. Sonnet 5.5 scores 46.2% at Max effort and 52.1% at Xhigh. Opus 5.5 scores 54.4%.
Anthropic says benchmarks show one part of a model, and that Opus 5.5 is still clearly stronger on complex, open-ended work that needs sustained judgment.
The catch is the token bill
You pay per token. So the number of tokens a model spends on a job matters as much as the rate.
According to Anthropic, Sonnet 5.5 has the same rate as Sonnet 5 and uses fewer tokens on the same work. Early customers put numbers on it.
- Balyasny Asset Management ran 2,441 finance tasks. Sonnet 5.5 used about 121,000 tokens per answer. Sonnet 5 used 497,000.
- Box saw Sonnet 5.5 run 2.4 times faster than its previous model, with 12% fewer tokens.
- Slack saw about 14% fewer output tokens on its Slackbot evaluations.
- Lovable saw a third fewer tool calls.

Anthropic published and chose those figures. Artificial Analysis, an independent benchmarking site, shows a different picture at the top setting. In its setup all three models run at Max effort on the same 10 evaluations, and it reports what each one costs.
- Opus 5.5 scores 58, ranks first of 216 models, writes 260 million output tokens and costs $5.98 per task.
- Sonnet 5.5 scores 56, ranks third, writes 410 million output tokens and costs $7.60 per task.
- Sonnet 5 scores 38, writes 370 million output tokens and costs $5.09 per task.

At Max effort, Sonnet 5.5 costs 27% more per task than Opus 5.5 and 49% more than Sonnet 5. Both sets of numbers can be true, because they measure different effort settings. Anthropic's charts show the savings at Low, Medium and High effort. Anthropic says Sonnet 5.5 at Medium beats Sonnet 5's best Terminal-Bench score for less than a tenth of the cost per task. At the higher settings, it says the two Claude models cost a similar amount.

So effort decides your bill. Claude Code and the Claude apps default to Medium. The API defaults to High. Lower settings answer faster and use fewer tokens. Higher settings reason for longer and check more.

If you work at Medium, Sonnet 5.5 is the cheap model. If you would run it at Max, price Opus 5.5 at Max too and compare the two bills. For research and first drafts, stay at Medium. Save Max for the last pass.
Where it slips
Anthropic's system card for Sonnet 5.5 is direct about the weak spots.

It hallucinates more than Opus 5.5. On a closed-book factual test with no web search, it gets more answers right than Sonnet 5 and is slightly more likely to state a wrong one. Its net score is 0.35, ahead of Sonnet 5 and behind every other Claude model in the chart. The same card says it is more honest than Opus 5.5 when a user pushes back on it.

It takes more steps. On Toolathlon-Verified, 108 real tool-use tasks across more than 600 tools, Sonnet 5.5 passes 77.8% of tasks, the same as Opus 5.5. It needs 31.6 turns per task on average. Opus 5.5 needs 26.9.

And its knowledge stops in June 2026. For anyone who makes content, that gives one rule. Never ask a model what is trending. It answers from memory, and a model that hallucinates more is more likely to answer wrong. Give it data.
What it is good at

- Writing. Anthropic says it writes more clearly than the previous generation, so drafts need less cleanup. Every, one of the launch customers, says it has some of Opus 5.5's natural writing upgrades.

- Documents and slides. In one internal test, Anthropic gave it a public company's quarterly earnings materials, the call transcripts and a slide template, and asked for a 10-slide operating review. Two experts judged the first draft ready to send as is.
- Tool use. It matches Opus 5.5 on Toolathlon, and that is the skill you need when a model calls a data source and reads what comes back.

My routing rule is this. Use Sonnet 5.5 at Medium effort for well-scoped work you repeat, such as tagging videos, writing hook variants, drafting scripts, cleaning transcripts and research passes that call tools. Use Opus 5.5 when the job is open-ended and you want the model to make judgment calls, such as positioning or a full content strategy.
A live test on content about Claude

A disclosure before the test. I co-founded Virlo. It tracks short-form video on TikTok, Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts. I used its data for this test because it lets me ask what is working right now, with the source video attached to every answer.

The setup was Claude Code with the model set to Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Virlo's MCP server connected. I asked it about the tech category, because that is where people talk about Claude. It made four data calls. One was free and three cost $0.25 each, so the run cost $0.75 in Virlo credits. The results came to roughly 25,000 tokens by my estimate, which is about five cents of input at Sonnet 5.5's price.

One term first. Virality Score compares a video's views with its creator's follower count, so a 5,000 follower account and a 5 million follower account sit on one scale. Virlo reads 35 and above as exceptional, 25 to 35 as very strong and 18 to 25 as strong. A strong hit means a score of 18 or more.
Finding 1. The most used hook types in tech are among the weakest
The free call returned every hook type in tech across 75,895 videos, from Virlo's snapshot on 28 September 2026.

Tutorial promises, the "three things you can do with X" kind, are 29.9% of tech videos. Bold claims are 27.2%. Together that is 57.0% of the category. They hit 15.8% and 12.7% of the time, and 14.3% combined.

Comparison hooks are 1.1% of tech videos and hit 25.9% of the time. POV setups are 2.0% and hit 23.5%. A comparison hook is about 1.8 times as likely to be a strong hit as a tutorial promise or a bold claim.
Finding 2. What winning hooks that name Claude look like

Virlo's index has 31 English video hooks that name Claude. I pulled the top 30 by Virality Score. Twenty-nine of them score above 35. The other one is the single word "claude", which 20 different posts use as their opening line, and it scores 34.4. Between them the 30 got 139.8 million views.

The accounts are small. The median has 6,509 followers, and 24 of the 30 have fewer than 25,000. The best ratio belongs to @magnettick, with 904 followers and 2.97 million views on "How it feels prompting Chatgpt to make a prompt for Claude code". That is 3,289 views for every follower.
Five patterns show up.

1. A reaction to a capability. "Excuse me?! Claude can do WHAT now?!", "im sorry... claude mythos can do what now??" and "CLAUDE can do WHAT???". All three are questions on TikTok from accounts under 3,700 followers, and they got 2.47 million views between them.
2. "Someone built". Three near-identical hooks about a digital whip that makes Claude respond faster. Three accounts told the same story, and the three got 21.1 million views between them.

3. Model against model. Four hooks put Claude next to ChatGPT, Gemini, Cursor or Kimi. One runs the same engine simulation prompt on four models and prints the price of each run. Another asks "who won??" over a coding prompt and got 10.2 million views on a 7,950 follower account. The four total 15.1 million views.

4. An experiment with Claude. "I gave Claude my salary and career history. It showed me income opportunities I did not know I was sitting on." got 2.23 million views on 6,422 followers. Four hooks use this shape, in first person or as a what-if, and they total 7.75 million views.

5. A numbered promise. "If you have a Mac, here are three things you can do with Claude that will save you a ton of time and money" got 47.9 million views on 87,601 followers, the most of the 30. "3 mindblowing yet simple Claude Cowork agents" got 26.3 million. Those two make up 53% of all the views in the set.

Twenty-seven of the 30 open with on-screen text, not a person speaking. Ten are 8 seconds long or shorter. The median hook is 13 words. Only one names a Claude model version, Claude Opus 4.7, inside a price comparison. None leads with a benchmark score.
Finding 3. What happened to Opus 5.5 launch week
Opus 5.5 launched on 22 September. Virlo's index has 16 English video hooks that name it, all published from 22 to 24 September. They have 358,256 views between them, and the best one got 128,562.

Eight of the 15 that have a score are positive, which means the video got more views than the account has followers. One reached 25, the very strong line. It was "OPUS 5.5 IS WAY SMARTER AND CHEAPER THAN ASTRA 6", from an account with 6,710 followers.
Three differences separate the top of the list from the bottom.

- Account size. The three accounts with more than 100,000 followers all scored below zero. The largest, with 623,135 followers, got 1,882 views. The median follower count is 2,737 for the eight highest scores and 37,300 for the seven lowest.
- A rival in the first line. Seven of the eight highest-scoring hooks name GPT-6, Astra or OpenAI next to Opus 5.5. One of the seven lowest does.

- The opening. The four lowest scores all start with a long spoken intro, like "breaking news again another launch Opus 5.5 is here so in this video I'm gonna get right into it". The best ones are a line of on-screen text. "GPT-6 Sol VS Claude Opus 5.5" is six words.

Sixteen hooks is a small sample, and Virlo's index does not capture every video. Treat this as a pattern to test, not a rule. Sonnet 5.5 launched on 28 September, so the same launch-week conditions apply now.
What Sonnet 5.5 did with the data
I gave it the three questions and it picked the calls. It made the free taxonomy call first, then the two phrase searches, then a pull of this week's tech hooks. It stopped at four calls.
Four points from its read of the results are worth keeping.

1. Hook type is not what separated the winners. Bold claims, tutorial promises and questions make up 20 of the 30 Claude hooks, close to their 70.7% share of tech videos. What separates the winners is the subject, which is a reaction, a comparison, an experiment or a number.
2. Three of the 30 are one story. The digital whip hooks tell a single news item three times, and all three score above 53.
3. Comparison and POV hooks are 3.0% of tech videos and 13% of the 30 strongest Claude hooks. That matches the hit rates from the free call.
4. The Opus 5.5 sample is too small to rank hook types. It compared account size, rival mentions and opening style, and it said so.
Then I asked it for five hooks for a post about Sonnet 5.5, each borrowing one structure from the results. This is what it wrote.
1. Reaction: "Claude Sonnet 5.5 scores 1844. Opus 5.5 scores 1846. It costs half as much per token. Excuse me?!"
2. News relay: "Anthropic just shipped a Claude that costs half as much per token as Opus 5.5 and scores within 2 points of it on real work tasks."
3. Model against model: "Claude Sonnet 5.5 vs Opus 5.5. Same jobs. Half the price per token."
4. Experiment: "I gave Claude Sonnet 5.5 30 viral hooks and asked what they have in common."
5. What-if: "What happens if you ask Claude Sonnet 5.5 to write your hooks from real TikTok data?"
None of them copies a real hook. Each one borrows a structure and puts the news inside it.

Sonnet 5.5 also built the video below, a 15 second motion graphics spot, from a single prompt. Every scene is code it wrote, on real data and real product footage. The animation engine came from earlier videos. Sonnet 5.5 wrote the scenes, the timing and the sound edit.
Run it yourself

Connect Virlo. virlo.ai/mcp has a Set up with Claude button that opens Virlo in Claude's directory and connects it to Claude Desktop, claude.ai or Claude Code. If you prefer an API key, create one at dev.virlo.ai. The same server works in Cursor, VS Code and Windsurf.
Then pick Claude Sonnet 5.5 in the model menu and leave effort on Medium. Paste these prompts one at a time.
Prompt 1. Which hook types win in your category
Use Virlo. Call get_hook_types for the category [your category], sorted by strong_hit_rate.
Ignore any hook type with fewer than 500 videos.
Show me which hook types are used most and which ones hit most, and tell me where the two lists disagree.
Prompt 2. What winning hooks about your subject look like
Use Virlo. Run search_hooks for the phrase "[your product or topic]" in English.
Then run get_trending_hooks for [your category] over the last 7 days.
Group the results by pattern, not by hook type. For each pattern, give the count, the verbatim hooks, the follower counts and the views.
Tell me which patterns come from accounts under 25,000 followers, and say how large the sample is.
Prompt 3. Write the hooks
Write 10 hooks for [my post]. Each one borrows a structure from the results, never the words.
Label each hook with the pattern it borrows and the source hook. Keep every hook under 15 words.
The first prompt is free. Each search costs $0.25, and you don't need a Virlo subscription to use the API.
What a sceptic would say

The benchmarks are Anthropic's. Artificial Analysis is the first independent check, and it puts Sonnet 5.5 third of 216 models. It also shows the token use. Give the model a few weeks of real use before you decide.

The two cost numbers disagree until you separate the effort settings. If you only read Anthropic's page, you will think Sonnet 5.5 is always cheaper. If you only read Artificial Analysis, you will think it is not. Test your own workload at the effort you will use.

The Virlo samples are small. Thirty hooks and sixteen hooks are enough to spot a pattern and not enough to prove one. Both come from Virlo's index, which does not capture every video. The index returned only 31 hooks that name Claude, and 29 of the 30 I read score above 35. That looks like a list weighted toward winners, so read Finding 2 as what winning Claude hooks look like, not what the average Claude video does.
The analysis was written by the model. Every number in this article comes from a tool call or from a source page, and the sources are listed at the end.
And I built Virlo. I said so above.
FAQs
Is Sonnet 5.5 free?
Anthropic says anyone can chat with it on Claude.ai. On the API it costs $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens.
Should I move everything from Opus 5.5?
No. Try Sonnet 5.5 on one job you repeat, at Medium effort, and compare the bills. Keep Opus 5.5 for open-ended work that needs judgment.
Does it work in Claude Code?
Yes. Medium is the default effort there.
What about Haiku 5.5?
Anthropic says it joins the family in the coming weeks.
What does the Virlo data cost?
The hook type call is free. Each hook search is $0.25.
Which platforms does Virlo cover?
TikTok, Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts.
What to do this week
- Move one research or drafting prompt to Sonnet 5.5 at Medium effort and compare it against what you use now, on the same job.
- Give it data. What it says about trends from memory is a guess, and its knowledge stops in June 2026.
- If you post about Sonnet 5.5, put a rival or a number in the first line, and put it on screen. Opus 5.5 week suggests small accounts move first.
- Check your hook against your category before you post.
Start for $0: virlo.ai
Add Virlo to Claude: virlo.ai/mcp
Reply with your niche. I'll run the hook check through Sonnet 5.5 for the first ten replies and post what wins.
If this was useful, repost it so someone else finds it.
Sources
- Anthropic, "Introducing Claude Sonnet 5.5" and the Claude Sonnet 5.5 system card, 28 September 2026.
- Artificial Analysis model pages for Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5, read 28 September 2026.
- Virlo's MCP server, run on 28 September 2026 in Claude Code on Claude Sonnet 5.5. The 27% and 49% figures, the totals, the medians and the cluster sums are my arithmetic on the returned data.
